description: multidisciplinary team of passionate and innovative individuals with a shared interest in technology, science, and space exploration
summary:
Fire-Zer is a web observatory that turns two decades of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent, comparable record for Indonesia. NASA's MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) sensors detect fires very differently: VIIRS sees roughly twice as many fire pixels, so naively joining their records creates a false upward trend. We built a harmonization pipeline that grids FIRMS detections into ~1 km fire-cell-days and calibrates MODIS to VIIRS-equivalent units using tile- and month-specific ratios. In leave-one-year-out validation (2013–2025), harmonization cut median monthly error from 73% (raw MODIS) to 11%, with uncertainty intervals shown on every estimate.

The interactive app presents this 2003–present record for Riau, Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra, and all of Indonesia: a month-by-month heatmap, seasonal comparison against a fixed 2003–2025 climatology, how unusual the latest month is (percentile), a raw-versus-harmonized sensor view, and CSV export. This matters because peatland fires in Indonesia drive regional haze, health crises, and major carbon emissions. A consistent long-term baseline lets researchers, policymakers, and the public tell real changes in fire activity from sensor artifacts.
details:
What it does and how it works

Fire-Zer combines 23 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire detections over Indonesia into a single consistent monthly record, then presents it through an interactive web observatory.

1. Data ingestion. We downloaded FIRMS archive and near-real-time data for Indonesia: MODIS Collection 6.1 (Terra + Aqua, 2003–present) and VIIRS 375 m Suomi-NPP Collection 2 (2012–present). This totals 5.69 million unique detections.

2. Cleaning. We removed non-vegetation detections (FIRMS type ≠ 0) and 703 persistent static heat sources such as industrial sites. Only daytime, nominal- or high-confidence detections are counted, so both sensors are compared under the same conditions.

3. Gridding. Detections are aggregated into ~1 km (0.01°) fire-cell-days. This reduces double-counting caused by the sensors' different pixel sizes.

4. Harmonization. VIIRS detects 3.0–3.9× more fire cells than MODIS. Simply joining the two records would create a false ~4.7× jump in 2012. Using the 2012–2025 overlap, we learn VIIRS/MODIS ratios per 1°×1° tile and calendar month, with a national fallback, and convert MODIS-era counts into VIIRS-equivalent fire cells.

5. Validation. In leave-one-year-out tests (2013–2025, 156 months), median monthly error was 11.1% with harmonization, versus 12.8% for a single constant ratio and 72.6% for raw MODIS. Every estimate carries a calibrated ~80% uncertainty interval.

6. Exploration. The web app shows:

- a 2003–present month-by-month heatmap;

- seasonal curves against a fixed 2003–2025 climatology (median and interquartile range);

- the latest complete month's percentile ("how unusual is now?");

- a raw-versus-harmonized sensor comparison;

- CSV export.

It covers Riau, Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra, and all of Indonesia.

Benefits

- No false trends: fire activity can be compared across 2003–2026 without the 2012 sensor break.

- Honest uncertainty: intervals, missing-data hatching, and labels separating "observed zero" from "no data" prevent over-interpretation.

- Fast and accessible: the static deployment loads instantly in any browser, with no account required.

- Open and reproducible: every number traces back to public NASA FIRMS data through a documented, scripted pipeline.

Intended impact

Indonesia's peatland fires cause transboundary haze, respiratory illness, and large carbon emissions. The 2015 and 2019 seasons were among the worst on record. Fire-Zer gives researchers, local governments, journalists, and communities a trustworthy baseline to:

- judge whether a season is abnormal;

- evaluate fire-prevention policies over time;

- communicate risk using a single, consistent number.
